a11y.apg: No APG pattern, and that is the answer: it is a native <input>, so selection, editing, undo, autofill, the software keyboard and every input type the platform knows come from the browser. Wrapping it in Field is what gives it a name and ties hint and error through aria-describedby. A control that needs a role is not this one.
a11y.keyboardNote: Measured in a browser on 29/08/2026 (apps/keyboard-probe + tests/visual/teclado-motor.spec.ts). This ficha comes from the lineage that did not have check 30, so it declared keys with no measurement behind them — the merge of the two lineages on 29/08/2026 is what surfaced it. Confirmed: nothing beyond the platform's own. Tab and Shift+Tab are out of the count on both sides by construction: Tab moves focus anywhere on a page, so it never distinguishes one component from another. What this measurement establishes is that there is no ENGINE keyboard here to measure — the keyboard is the document order, which is the correct answer for this component. (Space is also out of the count in a text field: the space bar types a space and changes the value, so the snapshot would see a change for any printable key.)

props.name: type
props.description: Native type. date, time, color and file use the browser's own widget, themed by tokens.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or uncontrolled, as in plain React. The component adds no state of its own.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: An example of the value, never a substitute for the label.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Native disabled: skipped by the keyboard and not submitted.

props.name: formatOnBlur
props.description: Normalises the value AFTER focus leaves the field — a licence plate, a document number, a phone. It deliberately does not mask while you type: the USWDS ships its input mask with a recorded WCAG 2.1 AA failure, MUI dropped masked date fields in v6 because the text leaks between sections, and a live mask makes the screen reader announce what was typed while the field shows something else. Aurea supplies the moment; the format stays yours, because plates and documents are country rules. The formatted text becomes the element's own value — nothing is painted over it — and your onChange is called with it, so controlled fields work.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes on the field. Every native attribute of the element passes through: name, required, autoComplete, pattern, min/max, and the rest.

props.name: size
props.description: The system's size step (sm/md/lg), NOT the HTML size attribute — that one is a width in characters and it is deliberately shadowed here, because two meanings for one prop name is worse than losing the native one.
